preamble: A palatalized dental/alveolar stop [dʲ] can be reanalysed as a true palatal stop [ɟ] when the secondary palatal gesture becomes the primary place of articulation. Czech and Slovak did this with the palatalized dentals that arose before front vowels in Late Common Slavic: Proto-Slavic *d before front vowels now surfaces as palatal ⟨ď⟩ [ɟ]. Recasens (2020) treats such (alveolo)palatal stops as the typical intermediate stage in the palatalization of dentoalveolars.

examples.note: 'grandfather'; the dental was palatalized before *ě (cf. Russian дед [dʲet], which keeps [dʲ]), and Czech turned it into the palatal stop ⟨ď⟩/⟨dě⟩ [ɟ].
'day'; cf. Russian день [dʲenʲ] with palatalized [dʲ], where Slovak has the palatal stop /ɟ/.
